2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection for RefractRouter v0.1

Executive Summary

RefractRouter v0.1 requires a reproducible per-node model router on top of a fixed task DAG, so platform choice is driven by control rather than convenience. LangGraph is the recommended core substrate because it already provides the explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing the router depends on [source_002]. DeepAgents is built on LangGraph [source_001], so DeepSeek Harness is reserved for the outer validation environment [source_004]. The benchmark must report quality, cost, and critical-path latency under reproducible conditions [source_007].

Background

Existing routing work selects one model per request, while RefractRouter studies per-node selection against a fixed DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier [source_005]. Static task decomposition stays at the application layer: the router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred until node-level routing is validated [source_006]. These constraints frame the platform requirements.

Selection Criteria

The v0.1 criteria are fixed-DAG execution, per-node model routing, typed I/O, and an outer validation environment. A useful routing benchmark needs fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, and it should stay small enough to reproduce [source_007]. The scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure, readability, and HTML validity, with versioned prompts and rubrics attached to run records [source_008].

Platform Comparison

LangGraph offers a graph state machine framework with explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing [source_002], making it the strongest fit for the deterministic core loop. DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph that adds planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls [source_001]; for v0.1, autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled, so it is usable only as a fixed-DAG execution harness [source_001]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs [source_003], but v0.1 does not need it as a core dependency unless structured-output parsing becomes a measured bottleneck [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness is an agent harness where the agent loop itself is a plugin, so DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment rather than the routing core [source_004].

Risks

Adopting DeepAgents' higher-level ergonomics introduces planning variability that can conflict with a reproducible routing benchmark, so its optional features must stay disabled. Pulling in Pydantic AI prematurely adds surface area without a benchmark signal. Using DSH in the core loop would sacrifice determinism, while using it only in the outer validation environment preserves reproducibility [source_004]. Treating static decomposition as a router responsibility would blur the application-layer boundary [source_006].

Conclusion

For RefractRouter v0.1, LangGraph is the core routing substrate [source_002], DeepAgents is accepted only as a fixed-DAG harness with planning disabled [source_001], Pydantic AI is deferred [source_003], and DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment [source_004]. This layering preserves reproducibility for the benchmark, which must report quality, cost, and critical-path latency [source_007] under versioned scoring rubrics [source_008].

References

Evidence is drawn from platform documentation for DeepAgents [source_001], LangGraph [source_002], Pydantic AI [source_003], and DeepSeek Harness [source_004], together with the LLM routing research gap [source_005], the task decomposition boundary [source_006], the benchmark design note [source_007], and the v0.1 scoring rubric [source_008].

Existing routing work selects one model per request, while RefractRouter studies per-node selection against a fixed DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier [source_005]. Static task decomposition stays at the application layer: the router receives the DAG as input and focuses on per-node model selection, with dynamic re-splitting deferred until node-level routing is validated [source_006]. These constraints frame the platform requirements.

Selection Criteria

The v0.1 criteria are fixed-DAG execution, per-node model routing, typed I/O, and an outer validation environment. A useful routing benchmark needs fixed task DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency, and it should stay small enough to reproduce [source_007]. The scoring rubric weights requirement coverage, evidence accuracy, analysis depth, structure, readability, and HTML validity, with versioned prompts and rubrics attached to run records [source_008].

Platform Comparison

LangGraph offers a graph state machine framework with explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and check-pointing [source_002], making it the strongest fit for the deterministic core loop. DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph that adds planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls [source_001]; for v0.1, autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation should remain disabled, so it is usable only as a fixed-DAG execution harness [source_001]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured model outputs [source_003], but v0.1 does not need it as a core dependency unless structured-output parsing becomes a measured bottleneck [source_003]. DeepSeek Harness is an agent harness where the agent loop itself is a plugin, so DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment rather than the routing core [source_004].

Risks

Adopting DeepAgents' higher-level ergonomics introduces planning variability that can conflict with a reproducible routing benchmark, so its optional features must stay disabled. Pulling in Pydantic AI prematurely adds surface area without a benchmark signal. Using DSH in the core loop would sacrifice determinism, while using it only in the outer validation environment preserves reproducibility [source_004]. Treating static decomposition as a router responsibility would blur the application-layer boundary [source_006].

Conclusion

For RefractRouter v0.1, LangGraph is the core routing substrate [source_002], DeepAgents is accepted only as a fixed-DAG harness with planning disabled [source_001], Pydantic AI is deferred [source_003], and DSH is reserved for the outer validation environment [source_004]. This layering preserves reproducibility for the benchmark, which must report quality, cost, and critical-path latency [source_007] under versioned scoring rubrics [source_008].
